scope.flow: sUSDM ERC4626 share conversion and ERC20 decimals metadata
scope.environment: sUSDM vault over USDM (6-decimal asset) with _decimalsOffset()=6

statements.text: sUSDM is an ERC4626 vault over USDM and sets _decimalsOffset() to 6.
USDM uses 6 decimals because it is minted 1:1 against USDC.
With a 6-decimal asset and a 6-decimal offset, sUSDM shares are 12-decimal shares; depositing 1e6 USDM mints 1e12 sUSDM.
An external protocol interacting with sUSDM relies on susdm.decimals() to convert an sUSDM balance to USDC.
The current sUSDM implementation overrides decimals() to return 6, so share math uses 12 decimals while ERC20 metadata reports 6 decimals.
sUSDM.decimals() should report the same decimal precision used by sUSDM share math (12 decimals), matching the documented metadata.
A conversion of 1e12 sUSDM (1 sUSDM) to USDC using decimals() should yield 1e6 USDC units (1 USDC), not a value off by a factor of 1e6.

ambiguities: No explicit attacker action or transaction is described; the issue is a metadata/decimals mismatch observed by external integrations.
The report does not state that anyone can call decimals() or that an unauthorized caller condition exists.
The incorrect valuation is described as a potential consequence for external protocols, not an observed on-chain transaction.
